source: WHO Consolidated Guidelines on TB, Module 2, 2021
text: Tuberculosis (TB) is caused by the bacterium Mycobacterium tuberculosis. It most commonly affects the lungs (pulmonary TB) and is spread through the air when a person with active pulmonary TB coughs, sneezes, or spits. A person needs to inhale only a few of these germs to become infected. About one-quarter of the global population is estimated to have been infected with TB bacteria, but most people will not go on to develop TB disease.

provenance.source_document: WHO Consolidated Guidelines on TB, Module 2, 2021
provenance.note: Paraphrased for CHW decision support; not a verbatim WHO excerpt.

source: WHO TB Fact Sheet, 2024
text: Common symptoms of active pulmonary TB include a persistent cough (sometimes with blood or sputum), chest pain, weakness, fatigue, weight loss, fever, and night sweats. A cough lasting more than 2-3 weeks is a key indicator that should prompt investigation for TB, especially in high-burden settings.

provenance.source_document: WHO TB Fact Sheet, 2024
provenance.note: Paraphrased for CHW decision support; not a verbatim WHO excerpt.

source: WHO Consolidated Guidelines on TB, Module 2, 2021
text: Computer-aided detection (CAD) software for TB screening on chest X-rays has shown sensitivity comparable to human readers. CAD systems provide a probability score indicating the likelihood of TB-related abnormalities. These are screening tools — a positive screening result must always be followed by confirmatory bacteriological testing such as sputum smear microscopy, Xpert MTB/RIF, or culture.

provenance.source_document: WHO Consolidated Guidelines on TB, Module 2, 2021
provenance.note: Paraphrased for CHW decision support; not a verbatim WHO excerpt.

source: WHO Operational Handbook on TB, Module 2, 2021
text: When interpreting CAD screening results, a higher probability score indicates greater likelihood of TB-related abnormalities on the chest X-ray. However, the threshold for referral should be determined based on the local context, prevalence, and available confirmatory testing. No CAD system replaces the need for bacteriological confirmation of TB disease.

provenance.source_document: WHO Operational Handbook on TB, Module 2, 2021
provenance.note: Paraphrased for CHW decision support; not a verbatim WHO excerpt.

source: WHO Consolidated Guidelines on TB, Module 2, 2021
text: Patients with a positive TB screening result (high probability on CAD or abnormal chest X-ray) should be referred for confirmatory diagnostic testing. The recommended first-line confirmatory test is Xpert MTB/RIF, which simultaneously detects TB and rifampicin resistance. Where Xpert is unavailable, sputum smear microscopy should be performed. Referral should be prompt — delays in diagnosis increase transmission risk.

provenance.source_document: WHO Consolidated Guidelines on TB, Module 2, 2021
provenance.note: Paraphrased for CHW decision support; not a verbatim WHO excerpt.

source: WHO Operational Handbook on TB, Module 2, 2021
text: For patients with an indeterminate or borderline screening result, clinical judgement is needed. If symptoms persist (cough > 2 weeks, weight loss, night sweats), repeat the chest X-ray or proceed directly to sputum testing. If the patient is asymptomatic with a borderline result, schedule a follow-up screening in 2-4 weeks. Document the result and ensure the patient returns for follow-up.

provenance.source_document: WHO Operational Handbook on TB, Module 2, 2021
provenance.note: Paraphrased for CHW decision support; not a verbatim WHO excerpt.

source: WHO Operational Handbook on TB, Module 2, 2021
text: A negative screening result (low probability on CAD, normal chest X-ray) in an asymptomatic person suggests TB disease is unlikely at this time. However, advise the patient to return if they develop symptoms such as persistent cough, fever, weight loss, or night sweats. In high-burden settings, periodic screening may be recommended for high-risk groups including people living with HIV, household contacts of TB patients, and healthcare workers.

provenance.source_document: WHO Operational Handbook on TB, Module 2, 2021
provenance.note: Paraphrased for CHW decision support; not a verbatim WHO excerpt.

source: WHO Consolidated Guidelines on TB, Module 4, 2022
text: Drug-susceptible pulmonary TB is treated with a standard 6-month regimen: 2 months of isoniazid, rifampicin, pyrazinamide, and ethambutol (intensive phase), followed by 4 months of isoniazid and rifampicin (continuation phase). Treatment must be completed in full even if the patient feels better — incomplete treatment is a major driver of drug resistance. Directly observed therapy (DOT) is recommended to ensure adherence.

provenance.source_document: WHO Consolidated Guidelines on TB, Module 4, 2022
provenance.note: Paraphrased for CHW decision support; not a verbatim WHO excerpt.

source: WHO Patient Education Materials, 2023
text: TB is curable. With proper treatment, most people with TB recover fully. Treatment takes 6 months — it is important to take all medicines as prescribed, even after feeling better. Stopping treatment early can cause the disease to return in a drug-resistant form that is harder to treat. During treatment, cover your mouth when coughing, ensure good ventilation, and attend all follow-up appointments.

provenance.note: Paraphrased for CHW decision support; not a verbatim WHO excerpt.

source: WHO Patient Education Materials, 2023
text: A positive screening result does not mean you definitely have TB — it means further testing is needed. The screening uses artificial intelligence to check your chest X-ray for signs that could indicate TB. If additional tests confirm TB, treatment will be started. TB treatment is free in most countries through national TB programmes. Early detection and treatment save lives and prevent spread to family and community members.

provenance.note: Paraphrased for CHW decision support; not a verbatim WHO excerpt.

source: WHO Consolidated Guidelines on TB, Module 1, 2022
text: People living with HIV are at significantly higher risk of developing TB disease. TB is the leading cause of death among people with HIV. All people living with HIV should be regularly screened for TB. If TB is diagnosed, treatment should start immediately alongside antiretroviral therapy. TB preventive treatment (TPT) is recommended for people with HIV who do not have active TB.

provenance.note: Paraphrased for CHW decision support; not a verbatim WHO excerpt.

source: WHO TB Infection Prevention and Control, 2019
text: To reduce TB transmission in healthcare facilities: ensure adequate natural ventilation, implement cough etiquette (cover mouth when coughing), separate patients with suspected TB from others, use personal protective equipment (N95 respirators) when caring for TB patients, and minimize time spent in enclosed spaces with suspected TB patients. Early diagnosis and treatment initiation are the most effective infection control measures.

source: WHO Consolidated Guidelines on TB, Module 5, 2022
text: TB in children can be difficult to diagnose because children often cannot produce sputum and the disease may present differently than in adults. Chest X-ray screening combined with clinical assessment is particularly important for childhood TB. Children who are household contacts of a TB patient should be evaluated and may be candidates for TB preventive treatment. A shorter 4-month treatment regimen is now recommended for children with non-severe TB.

source: WHO Consolidated Guidelines on TB, Module 4, 2022
text: Drug-resistant TB (DR-TB) occurs when TB bacteria become resistant to the medicines used to treat them. Multidrug-resistant TB (MDR-TB) is resistant to at least isoniazid and rifampicin, the two most effective first-line drugs. DR-TB requires longer and more complex treatment regimens, often 9-18 months with second-line drugs that may have more side effects. Prevention of drug resistance depends on completing the full course of first-line treatment.

provenance.source_document: WHO Consolidated Guidelines on TB, Module 4, 2022
provenance.note: Paraphrased for CHW decision support; not a verbatim WHO excerpt.

source: WHO Consolidated Guidelines on TB, Module 4, 2022
text: When Xpert MTB/RIF detects rifampicin resistance, the patient should be referred to a facility equipped to manage DR-TB. Do not start standard first-line treatment if rifampicin resistance is detected. Second-line drugs include fluoroquinolones (levofloxacin, moxifloxacin), bedaquiline, and linezolid. Treatment must be supervised by a specialist team.

provenance.source_document: WHO Consolidated Guidelines on TB, Module 4, 2022
provenance.note: Paraphrased for CHW decision support; not a verbatim WHO excerpt.

source: WHO Operational Handbook on TB, Module 3, 2021
text: Sputum collection is essential for bacteriological confirmation of TB. Collect at least one sputum sample, ideally an early-morning specimen when bacterial load is highest. Instruct the patient to rinse their mouth with water, take a deep breath, cough deeply, and expectorate directly into the specimen container. Avoid saliva. If the patient cannot produce sputum, sputum induction with hypertonic saline may be attempted.

provenance.source_document: WHO Operational Handbook on TB, Module 3, 2021
provenance.note: Paraphrased for CHW decision support; not a verbatim WHO excerpt.

source: WHO Operational Handbook on TB, Module 3, 2021
text: Sputum samples should be processed as quickly as possible. If immediate processing is not available, store the specimen in a cool place (2-8 degrees Celsius) and transport it to the laboratory within 24-72 hours. Proper labeling with the patient name, date, and clinic is essential. Handle all specimens as potentially infectious — use standard biosafety precautions.

source: WHO Consolidated Guidelines on TB, Module 1, 2022
text: Contact investigation is a systematic process for identifying people exposed to a TB case. All household contacts of a person with bacteriologically confirmed pulmonary TB should be screened. Contacts who are symptomatic should be evaluated for active TB. Contacts who are asymptomatic, especially children under 5 and people living with HIV, should be offered TB preventive treatment (TPT) after ruling out active TB.

provenance.source_document: WHO Consolidated Guidelines on TB, Module 1, 2022
provenance.note: Paraphrased for CHW decision support; not a verbatim WHO excerpt.

source: WHO Consolidated Guidelines on TB, Module 1, 2022
text: TB preventive treatment (TPT) options include 6 months of isoniazid (6H), 3 months of isoniazid plus rifapentine (3HP), or 4 months of rifampicin (4R). TPT significantly reduces the risk of developing active TB in infected contacts. Adherence support and regular follow-up are important to ensure completion of preventive treatment.

provenance.source_document: WHO Consolidated Guidelines on TB, Module 1, 2022
provenance.note: Paraphrased for CHW decision support; not a verbatim WHO excerpt.

source: WHO TB Fact Sheet, 2024
text: TB prevention strategies include: BCG vaccination for infants in high-burden countries, TB preventive treatment for high-risk groups, infection control measures in healthcare facilities and congregate settings, active case finding to detect and treat infectious cases early, and improving general living conditions (nutrition, ventilation, reducing overcrowding).

provenance.source_document: WHO TB Fact Sheet, 2024
provenance.note: Paraphrased for CHW decision support; not a verbatim WHO excerpt.

source: WHO TB Fact Sheet, 2024
text: The BCG vaccine provides partial protection against severe forms of childhood TB (TB meningitis and miliary TB) but does not reliably prevent pulmonary TB in adults. BCG is recommended at birth or as soon as possible for all infants in TB-endemic countries. It is a one-time vaccination and does not require boosters.

provenance.source_document: WHO TB Fact Sheet, 2024
provenance.note: Paraphrased for CHW decision support; not a verbatim WHO excerpt.

source: WHO Consolidated Guidelines on TB, Module 3, 2021
text: A positive TB screening result (from chest X-ray or CAD) is not a confirmed diagnosis. Confirmation requires bacteriological testing: Xpert MTB/RIF (recommended first-line), sputum smear microscopy, or mycobacterial culture. Xpert MTB/RIF simultaneously detects TB and rifampicin resistance within 2 hours. A confirmed diagnosis means TB bacteria have been detected in a patient specimen.

provenance.source_document: WHO Consolidated Guidelines on TB, Module 3, 2021
provenance.note: Paraphrased for CHW decision support; not a verbatim WHO excerpt.

source: WHO Consolidated Guidelines on TB, Module 3, 2021
text: Clinical diagnosis (without bacteriological confirmation) may be necessary when sputum tests are negative but clinical suspicion remains high — for example, in children who cannot produce sputum, people living with HIV with atypical presentations, or extrapulmonary TB. Clinical diagnosis should be made by a qualified clinician based on clinical assessment, chest X-ray findings, and response to empiric treatment.

provenance.source_document: WHO Consolidated Guidelines on TB, Module 3, 2021
provenance.note: Paraphrased for CHW decision support; not a verbatim WHO excerpt.

source: WHO Consolidated Guidelines on TB, Module 4, 2022
text: Treatment adherence is critical for cure and preventing drug resistance. Directly observed therapy (DOT) means a trained observer watches the patient swallow each dose. Digital adherence technologies (video DOT, medication monitors, SMS reminders) are recommended alternatives where feasible. Common reasons for non-adherence include feeling better before treatment ends, side effects, distance to health facility, stigma, and economic burden.

provenance.source_document: WHO Consolidated Guidelines on TB, Module 4, 2022
provenance.note: Paraphrased for CHW decision support; not a verbatim WHO excerpt.

source: WHO Consolidated Guidelines on TB, Module 4, 2022
text: Common side effects of first-line TB drugs include nausea, loss of appetite, joint pain, orange-colored urine (harmless, from rifampicin), and tingling in hands or feet (peripheral neuropathy from isoniazid). Serious side effects requiring immediate attention include yellowing of eyes or skin (hepatotoxicity), vision changes, severe rash, and persistent vomiting. Patients should be counseled on expected side effects before starting treatment.

provenance.source_document: WHO Consolidated Guidelines on TB, Module 4, 2022
provenance.note: Paraphrased for CHW decision support; not a verbatim WHO excerpt.

source: WHO Consolidated Guidelines on TB, Module 2, 2021
text: Ikọ́ fée fée (TB) jẹ́ àrùn tí bakitéríà Mycobacterium tuberculosis ń fa. Ó máa ń kọlu ẹ̀dọ̀fóró jùlọ. Ó ń tàn nípasẹ̀ afẹ́fẹ́ nígbà tí ẹni tí ó ní TB bá kọ́ tàbí sín. Nǹkan bíi ìdá mẹ́rin àwọn ènìyàn lágbàyé ti gba àkóràn TB, àmọ́ ọ̀pọ̀lọpọ̀ kò ní ṣàìsàn.

provenance.source_document: WHO Consolidated Guidelines on TB, Module 2, 2021
provenance.note: Paraphrased for CHW decision support; not a verbatim WHO excerpt.

source: WHO TB Fact Sheet, 2024
text: Àwọn àmì àrùn TB pẹ̀lú ikọ́ tí kò fẹ́ dáké (nígbà mìíràn pẹ̀lú ẹ̀jẹ̀), irora àyà, àìlera, dídínwúwó, ibà, àti laálàá lóru. Ikọ́ tí ó ju ọ̀sẹ̀ 2-3 lọ yẹ kí a ṣèwádìí fún TB.

provenance.source_document: WHO TB Fact Sheet, 2024
provenance.note: Paraphrased for CHW decision support; not a verbatim WHO excerpt.

source: WHO Consolidated Guidelines on TB, Module 4, 2022
text: Ìtọ́jú TB tí kò lè ṣàtakò oògùn ń gba oṣù 6: oṣù 2 pẹ̀lú oògùn mẹ́rin (isoniazid, rifampicin, pyrazinamide, ethambutol), lẹ́yìn náà oṣù 4 pẹ̀lú oògùn méjì. A gbọ́dọ̀ parí ìtọ́jú náà ní kíkún.

provenance.source_document: WHO Consolidated Guidelines on TB, Module 4, 2022
provenance.note: Paraphrased for CHW decision support; not a verbatim WHO excerpt.

source: WHO Consolidated Guidelines on TB, Module 1, 2022
text: Àwọn ènìyàn tí ó ń gbé pẹ̀lú HIV wà ní ewu gíga láti ní àrùn TB. TB ni ohun tí ó ń pa àwọn tí ó ní HIV jùlọ. A gbọ́dọ̀ ṣe àyẹ̀wò TB fún gbogbo àwọn tí ó ní HIV láìsí ìdádúró.

provenance.source_document: WHO Consolidated Guidelines on TB, Module 1, 2022
provenance.note: Paraphrased for CHW decision support; not a verbatim WHO excerpt.

source: WHO Consolidated Guidelines on TB, Module 5, 2022
text: TB nínú àwọn ọmọdé ṣòro láti ṣe àyẹ̀wò nítorí wọn kò lè tu sputum jáde. Fọ́tò àyà àti ìdánwò dókítà ṣe pàtàkì. Àwọn ọmọdé tí wọ́n bá pẹ́ pẹ̀lú ẹni tí ó ní TB yẹ kí a ṣe àyẹ̀wò wọn.

provenance.source_document: WHO Consolidated Guidelines on TB, Module 5, 2022
provenance.note: Paraphrased for CHW decision support; not a verbatim WHO excerpt.

source: WHO TB Infection Prevention and Control, 2019
text: Láti dín ìtànkálẹ̀ TB kù ní ilé ìwòsàn: rí i pé afẹ́fẹ́ ń gbé lọ dáadáa, bo ẹnu nígbà tí o bá ń kọ́, ya àwọn tí wọ́n ní àrùn TB sọ́tọ̀, lo ohun ìdáàbòbò bíi N95. Ìdánilẹ́kọ̀ọ́ tètè àti ìtọ́jú ni ohun tí ó dára jùlọ.

provenance.source_document: WHO TB Infection Prevention and Control, 2019
provenance.note: Paraphrased for CHW decision support; not a verbatim WHO excerpt.

source: WHO Consolidated Guidelines on TB, Module 4, 2022
text: TB tí kò gbọ́ oògùn mọ́ (DR-TB) máa ń wáyé nígbà tí bakitéríà TB bá di aláìgbọ́ oògùn. MDR-TB kò gbọ́ isoniazid àti rifampicin. Ìdènà rẹ̀ ni láti parí ìtọ́jú àkọ́kọ́ ní kíkún. Ìtọ́jú DR-TB ń gba oṣù 9-18.

provenance.source_document: WHO Consolidated Guidelines on TB, Module 4, 2022
provenance.note: Paraphrased for CHW decision support; not a verbatim WHO excerpt.

source: WHO Operational Handbook on TB, Module 3, 2021
text: Àyẹ̀wò sputum ṣe pàtàkì fún ìdánilójú TB. Kó sputum ní kùtùkùtù àárọ̀. Sọ fún aláìsàn láti fi ẹnu gbá omi, mí ẹ̀mí jìn, kọ́ dáadáa, kí ó sì tu sínú ìgò ìdánwò. Yẹra fún ìtọ́ lásán.

provenance.source_document: WHO Operational Handbook on TB, Module 3, 2021
provenance.note: Paraphrased for CHW decision support; not a verbatim WHO excerpt.

source: WHO Consolidated Guidelines on TB, Module 1, 2022
text: A gbọ́dọ̀ ṣe àyẹ̀wò gbogbo àwọn ènìyàn tí ó bá ẹni tí ó ní TB gbé papọ̀. Àwọn tí ó ní àmì àrùn yẹ kí a ṣe ìdánwò wọn. Àwọn ọmọdé àti àwọn tí ó ní HIV lè gba ìtọ́jú ìdènà TB (TPT).

provenance.source_document: WHO Consolidated Guidelines on TB, Module 1, 2022
provenance.note: Paraphrased for CHW decision support; not a verbatim WHO excerpt.

source: WHO TB Fact Sheet, 2024
text: Àwọn ọ̀nà ìdènà TB pẹ̀lú: àjẹsára BCG fún àwọn ọmọ ìkókó, ìtọ́jú ìdènà fún àwọn tí ó wà ní ewu, ìṣàkóso àkóràn ní ilé ìwòsàn, wíwá àwọn ẹni tí ó ní àrùn tètè, àti ìmúdára ìgbé ayé (oúnjẹ, afẹ́fẹ́, dídín ìpọ́jù ènìyàn kù).

provenance.source_document: WHO TB Fact Sheet, 2024
provenance.note: Paraphrased for CHW decision support; not a verbatim WHO excerpt.

source: WHO Consolidated Guidelines on TB, Module 3, 2021
text: Àbájáde àyẹ̀wò TB tó dára kìí ṣe àyẹ̀wò tí a ti fìdí rẹ̀ múlẹ̀. Ìdánilójú nílò àyẹ̀wò sputum bíi Xpert MTB/RIF tàbí microscopy. Àyẹ̀wò Xpert ń rí TB àti àtakò rifampicin nínú wákàtí 2.

provenance.source_document: WHO Consolidated Guidelines on TB, Module 3, 2021
provenance.note: Paraphrased for CHW decision support; not a verbatim WHO excerpt.

source: WHO Consolidated Guidelines on TB, Module 4, 2022
text: Ìfaramọ́ ìtọ́jú ṣe pàtàkì fún ìwòsàn àti ìdènà àtakò oògùn. DOT túmọ̀ sí pé aláṣẹ kan yóò wò ó bí aláìsàn ṣe ń gbé oògùn. Àwọn ìdí tí ó ń mú kí ènìyàn má parí ìtọ́jú pẹ̀lú: ìrí ìwòsàn kí ìtọ́jú parí, àwọn ipa oògùn, àti ìjìnnà sí ilé ìwòsàn.

provenance.source_document: WHO Consolidated Guidelines on TB, Module 4, 2022
provenance.note: Paraphrased for CHW decision support; not a verbatim WHO excerpt.

source: WHO Consolidated Guidelines on TB, Module 2, 2021
text: Cutar tarin fuka (TB) kwayar cuta ce da ake kira Mycobacterium tuberculosis ke haddasa ta. Yawanci tana shafar huhu. Tana yaduwa ta iska lokacin da mai cutar ya yi tari ko atishawa. Kimanin kashi ɗaya cikin huɗu na mutane a duniya suna dauke da kwayar TB.

provenance.source_document: WHO Consolidated Guidelines on TB, Module 2, 2021
provenance.note: Paraphrased for CHW decision support; not a verbatim WHO excerpt.

source: WHO TB Fact Sheet, 2024
text: Alamomin cutar TB sun haɗa da tari mai ɗorewa (wani lokaci da jini), ciwon ƙirji, gajiya, raguwar nauyi, zazzabi, da zufa da daddare. Tari da ya wuce mako 2-3 ya kamata a bincika don TB.

provenance.source_document: WHO TB Fact Sheet, 2024
provenance.note: Paraphrased for CHW decision support; not a verbatim WHO excerpt.

source: WHO Consolidated Guidelines on TB, Module 4, 2022
text: Maganin TB da ba ta iya juriya ga magani ba yana ɗaukar watanni 6: watanni 2 tare da magunguna 4 (isoniazid, rifampicin, pyrazinamide, ethambutol), sai watanni 4 da magunguna 2. Dole ne a kammala maganin gaba ɗaya.

provenance.source_document: WHO Consolidated Guidelines on TB, Module 4, 2022
provenance.note: Paraphrased for CHW decision support; not a verbatim WHO excerpt.

source: WHO Consolidated Guidelines on TB, Module 1, 2022
text: Mutanen da ke zaune da HIV suna cikin babbar haɗari na kamuwa da cutar TB. TB ita ce babbar sanadin mutuwa a tsakanin masu HIV. Dole ne a yi wa dukkan mutanen da ke da HIV gwajin TB akai-akai.

provenance.source_document: WHO Consolidated Guidelines on TB, Module 1, 2022
provenance.note: Paraphrased for CHW decision support; not a verbatim WHO excerpt.

source: WHO Consolidated Guidelines on TB, Module 5, 2022
text: TB a cikin yara na iya wahalar ganewarsa saboda yara ba sa iya fitar da miyau. Hoton kirji da gwajin likita suna da muhimmanci. Ya kamata a duba yaran da suka zama tare da mai cutar TB kuma a ba su maganin rigakafi idan ya dace.

provenance.source_document: WHO Consolidated Guidelines on TB, Module 5, 2022
provenance.note: Paraphrased for CHW decision support; not a verbatim WHO excerpt.

source: WHO TB Infection Prevention and Control, 2019
text: Don rage yaduwar TB a asibitoci: tabbatar da samun iska mai kyau, rufe baki lokacin tari, raba marasa lafiya masu TB daga sauran, amfani da kayan kariya kamar abin rufe fuska N95. Ganowa da magani da wuri su ne mafi kyawun hanyoyin kariya.

provenance.source_document: WHO TB Infection Prevention and Control, 2019
provenance.note: Paraphrased for CHW decision support; not a verbatim WHO excerpt.

source: WHO Consolidated Guidelines on TB, Module 4, 2022
text: TB mai juriya ga magani (DR-TB) tana faruwa ne idan kwayoyin cutar TB suka ƙi karɓar magani. MDR-TB ba ta karɓar isoniazid da rifampicin. Maganin DR-TB yana ɗaukar watanni 9-18. Kammala maganin da aka fara shi ne hanyar rigakafi.

provenance.source_document: WHO Consolidated Guidelines on TB, Module 4, 2022
provenance.note: Paraphrased for CHW decision support; not a verbatim WHO excerpt.

source: WHO Operational Handbook on TB, Module 3, 2021
text: Tattara miyau yana da muhimmanci don tabbatar da cutar TB. A tattara miyau da safe-safe lokacin da kwayoyin cutar suka fi yawa. A umurci majiyyaci ya wanke baki, ya ɗauki numfashi mai zurfi, ya yi tari ƙwarai, ya tofa a cikin kwalba.

provenance.source_document: WHO Operational Handbook on TB, Module 3, 2021
provenance.note: Paraphrased for CHW decision support; not a verbatim WHO excerpt.

source: WHO Consolidated Guidelines on TB, Module 1, 2022
text: Dole ne a tantance dukkan mutanen da suka zauna tare da mai cutar TB. Masu alamun cuta ya kamata a duba su. Yara ƙasa da shekaru 5 da mutanen da ke zaune da HIV za a iya ba su maganin rigakafin TB (TPT).

provenance.source_document: WHO Consolidated Guidelines on TB, Module 1, 2022
provenance.note: Paraphrased for CHW decision support; not a verbatim WHO excerpt.

source: WHO TB Fact Sheet, 2024
text: Hanyoyin rigakafin TB sun haɗa da: allurar BCG ga jarirai, maganin rigakafi ga masu haɗari, tsarin kariya a asibitoci, neman masu cutar da wuri, da inganta yanayin rayuwa (abinci, iska, rage cunkoso).

provenance.source_document: WHO TB Fact Sheet, 2024
provenance.note: Paraphrased for CHW decision support; not a verbatim WHO excerpt.

source: WHO Consolidated Guidelines on TB, Module 3, 2021
text: Sakamako mai kyau na tantancewa ba tabbataccen ganewar asali ba ne. Dole ne a tabbatar ta hanyar gwajin miyau kamar Xpert MTB/RIF ko microscopy. Xpert na gano TB da juriya ga rifampicin cikin sa'o'i 2.

provenance.source_document: WHO Consolidated Guidelines on TB, Module 3, 2021
provenance.note: Paraphrased for CHW decision support; not a verbatim WHO excerpt.

source: WHO Consolidated Guidelines on TB, Module 4, 2022
text: Bi da magani daidai yana da matuƙar muhimmanci don warkewa da hana juriya. DOT yana nufin wani ya kalli majiyyaci yana shan magani. Dalilan da ke sa mutane su daina magani sun haɗa da jin sauki kafin lokaci, illar magani, da nisa zuwa asibiti.

provenance.source_document: WHO Consolidated Guidelines on TB, Module 4, 2022
provenance.note: Paraphrased for CHW decision support; not a verbatim WHO excerpt.

source: WHO Consolidated Guidelines on TB, Module 2, 2021
text: Ọrịa ụkwara nta nta (TB) bụ nje Mycobacterium tuberculosis na-ebute ya. Ọ na-emetụta ngụkọta ume karịsịa. Ọ na-agbasa site n'ikuku mgbe onye nwere TB na-asụ ụkwara. Ihe dịka otu n'ime mmadụ anọ nwere nje TB, mana ọtụtụ adịghị arịa.

provenance.source_document: WHO Consolidated Guidelines on TB, Module 2, 2021
provenance.note: Paraphrased for CHW decision support; not a verbatim WHO excerpt.

source: WHO TB Fact Sheet, 2024
text: Mgbaàmà ọrịa TB gụnyere ụkwara na-adịgide (mgbe ụfọdụ na ọbara), mgbu obi, ike ọgwụgwụ, belata ibu, ahụ ọkụ, na ọsụsọ n'abalị. Ụkwara gara izu 2-3 kwesịrị ka a nyochaa maka TB.

provenance.source_document: WHO TB Fact Sheet, 2024
provenance.note: Paraphrased for CHW decision support; not a verbatim WHO excerpt.

source: WHO Consolidated Guidelines on TB, Module 4, 2022
text: Ọgwụgwọ TB na-ewe ọnwa 6: ọnwa 2 nke ọgwụ anọ (isoniazid, rifampicin, pyrazinamide, ethambutol), wee ọnwa 4 nke ọgwụ abụọ. Onye ọrịa ga-agwụcha ọgwụgwọ ahụ n'uju.

provenance.source_document: WHO Consolidated Guidelines on TB, Module 4, 2022
provenance.note: Paraphrased for CHW decision support; not a verbatim WHO excerpt.

source: WHO Consolidated Guidelines on TB, Module 1, 2022
text: Ndị bi na HIV nwere ihe ize ndụ dị elu ịnwe ọrịa TB. TB bụ ihe kachasị na-egbu ndị nwere HIV. A ga-enyocha ndị niile nwere HIV maka TB mgbe niile.

provenance.source_document: WHO Consolidated Guidelines on TB, Module 1, 2022
provenance.note: Paraphrased for CHW decision support; not a verbatim WHO excerpt.

source: WHO Consolidated Guidelines on TB, Module 5, 2022
text: TB n'ụmụaka na-esiri ike ịchọpụta n'ihi na ụmụaka enweghị ike ịtụpụta sputum. Foto obi na nyocha dọkịta dị mkpa. Ụmụaka bi n'otu ụlọ na onye nwere TB kwesịrị ka a nyochaa ha ma nye ha ọgwụ mgbochi TB.

provenance.source_document: WHO Consolidated Guidelines on TB, Module 5, 2022
provenance.note: Paraphrased for CHW decision support; not a verbatim WHO excerpt.

source: WHO TB Infection Prevention and Control, 2019
text: Iji belata mgbasa TB n'ụlọ ọgwụ: hụ na ikuku na-agbasa nke ọma, kpuchie ọnụ mgbe ị na-asụ ụkwara, kewapụ ndị nwere ike inwe TB, jiri ihe nchekwa dịka N95. Ịchọta ọrịa ngwa ngwa na ịmalite ọgwụgwọ bụ ụzọ kachasị mma.

provenance.source_document: WHO TB Infection Prevention and Control, 2019
provenance.note: Paraphrased for CHW decision support; not a verbatim WHO excerpt.

source: WHO Consolidated Guidelines on TB, Module 4, 2022
text: TB na-eguzogide ọgwụ (DR-TB) na-eme mgbe nje TB hapụrụ ịnabata ọgwụ. MDR-TB eguzogidere isoniazid na rifampicin. Ọgwụgwọ DR-TB na-ewe ọnwa 9-18. Ịgwụcha ọgwụgwọ mbụ bụ ụzọ ichegide ya.

provenance.source_document: WHO Consolidated Guidelines on TB, Module 4, 2022
provenance.note: Paraphrased for CHW decision support; not a verbatim WHO excerpt.

source: WHO Operational Handbook on TB, Module 3, 2021
text: Ịkpọkọta sputum dị mkpa maka ịkwado TB. Kpọkọta ya n'ụtụtụ. Gwa onye ọrịa ka ọ sachaa ọnụ ya, kuo ume nke ọma, sụọ ụkwara nke ukwu, wee tụpụta n'ime karama. Zere mmiri ọnụ naanị.

provenance.source_document: WHO Operational Handbook on TB, Module 3, 2021
provenance.note: Paraphrased for CHW decision support; not a verbatim WHO excerpt.

source: WHO Consolidated Guidelines on TB, Module 1, 2022
text: A ga-anyocha ndị niile bi n'otu ụlọ na onye nwere TB. Ndị nwere mgbaàmà kwesịrị ka a nyochaa ha. Ụmụaka dị n'okpuru afọ 5 na ndị nwere HIV nwere ike ịnata ọgwụ mgbochi TB (TPT).

provenance.source_document: WHO Consolidated Guidelines on TB, Module 1, 2022
provenance.note: Paraphrased for CHW decision support; not a verbatim WHO excerpt.

source: WHO TB Fact Sheet, 2024
text: Ụzọ ichegide TB gụnyere: agịga BCG maka ụmụ ọhụrụ, ọgwụ mgbochi maka ndị nọ n'ihe ize ndụ, usoro nchekwa na ụlọ ọgwụ, ịchọta ndị nwere ọrịa ngwa ngwa, na ịmelite ụdị ndụ (nri, ikuku, ibelata mkpọkọta mmadụ).

provenance.source_document: WHO TB Fact Sheet, 2024
provenance.note: Paraphrased for CHW decision support; not a verbatim WHO excerpt.

source: WHO Consolidated Guidelines on TB, Module 3, 2021
text: Nsonaazụ nyocha TB dị mma abụghị nkwenye. A ga-eme nyocha sputum dịka Xpert MTB/RIF ma ọ bụ microscopy iji kwado ya. Xpert na-achọpụta TB na nguzogide rifampicin n'ime awa 2.

provenance.source_document: WHO Consolidated Guidelines on TB, Module 3, 2021
provenance.note: Paraphrased for CHW decision support; not a verbatim WHO excerpt.

source: WHO Consolidated Guidelines on TB, Module 4, 2022
text: Ịnabata ọgwụgwọ dị oke mkpa maka ịgwọ ọrịa na ichegide nguzogide ọgwụ. DOT pụtara na onye a zụrụ azụ na-elekọta onye ọrịa ka ọ na-aṅụ ọgwụ. Ihe ndị na-eme ka ndị mmadụ akwụsị ọgwụgwọ gụnyere: ịdị mma tupu ọgwụgwọ gwụsịa, mmetụta ọgwụ, na ịnọ anya ụlọ ọgwụ.

provenance.source_document: WHO Consolidated Guidelines on TB, Module 4, 2022
provenance.note: Paraphrased for CHW decision support; not a verbatim WHO excerpt.
